title: Minimum Subarray Reverse Operations

monster.name: Parity Inversion Archon
monster.title: Shifter of Even and Odd Jump Bands
monster.defeatQuote: Shortest operations to shift the 1 to all target indices!

description: You are given an integer `n` and an integer `p` in the range `[0, n - 1]`. Representing an array `arr` of size `n` with 1 at index `p` and 0 elsewhere. You can reverse any subarray of length `k` not containing indices in `banned`. Return an array `ans` where `ans[i]` is the minimum number of reverse operations needed to bring 1 to index `i`, or -1 if impossible.
starterCode:
def minReverseOperations(n: int, p: int, banned: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    pass
solutionCode:
def minReverseOperations(n: int, p: int, banned: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    from collections import deque
    ans = [-1] * n
    banned_set = set(banned)
    # Unvisited available nodes split by parity
    avail = {0: set(i for i in range(n) if i % 2 == 0 and i not in banned_set and i != p),
             1: set(i for i in range(n) if i % 2 == 1 and i not in banned_set and i != p)}
    q = deque([(p, 0)])
    ans[p] = 0
    while q:
        curr, d = q.popleft()
        # New positions after reversing subarray of length k covering curr
        min_j = max(0, curr - k + 1)
        max_j = min(n - k, curr)
        # Target range of curr reversed: 2*j + k - 1 - curr
        low = 2 * min_j + k - 1 - curr
        high = 2 * max_j + k - 1 - curr
        target_parity = (curr + k - 1) % 2
        to_remove = []
        for nxt in avail[target_parity]:
            if low <= nxt <= high:
                ans[nxt] = d + 1
                q.append((nxt, d + 1))
                to_remove.append(nxt)
        for r in to_remove:
            avail[target_parity].remove(r)
    return ans
hints: The reversed index range has the same parity (curr + k - 1) % 2. Prune visited nodes with sets.
